doc.title: Glenn Zottola interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 7, 2020

title: Lost groove in today's jazz; Snooky Young leading Sinatra's band
summary: Complaint that players today lack time and swing, with a memory of Snooky Young playing lead on Nelson Riddle charts with Sinatra.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: My complaint — let me just tell you my complaint about jazz today — to some degree, and they are great players these guys, they have lost the very thing we’re talking about. That time. That groove. That swing. All the guys playing with Ray Brown. All the guys I came up with — Milt Hinton — that’s what they loved about me because I absorbed that when I was a kid. I was listening to Louis’ records you know.
Does a person who’s teaching jazz, are they able to put that into words?
“You’re not swinging.” “Okay well if I’m not swinging how to I swing then?”

It’s hard. I mean you take a chart, and I’ve played in all the big bands you know. I remember doing Sinatra, playing with Sinatra and Snooky Young’s playing lead trumpet. And I’m playing next to him. I said oh my God, he’s playing these Nelson Riddle charts like nobody else. It was like being in a small quintet, Count Basie’s band but he’s playing Nelson Riddle charts with Sinatra. It was an awakening for me to hear him play lead with his concept as opposed to other great players who I played with — I played with Doc Severinsen you know.
Bobby Shew just talked about that.
Yes he is, he’s doing all right.
I knew he was ill you know. Okay.
